prompt: After the new till sent five sales with `amount` instead of `cents`, what did `totals.py` report?

choices.text: An error on the first sale without `cents`
choices.why: `.get` with a default never raises; that is the trouble.

choices.text: Twenty-five sales and the same totals as before
choices.why: Right. The count moved and the money did not, and nothing complained.

choices.text: Twenty sales, because the new ones were skipped
choices.why: They were counted: 25 sales. Only their money was missing.

choices.text: Recife's total five times too high
choices.why: Nothing was added for the new sales, so it stayed at 531.30.

prompt: JSON carries the name of every field in every message. Why does that not protect a reader from a renamed field?

choices.text: Kafka strips the names before storing the message
choices.why: The broker stores the bytes it was given, names and all.

choices.text: Names are carried, but no agreement about them is
choices.why: Right. A reader that misses a name gets nothing and carries on.

choices.text: JSON readers in Python cannot read nested objects
choices.why: Nesting has nothing to do with it; the field is at the top level.

choices.text: A rename changes the size of each message, which the consumer rejects
choices.why: Nothing was rejected; the reader read every sale.

prompt: A colleague proposes making `totals.py` try `cents`, then `amount`, then `price`. What is wrong with that fix, according to the section?

choices.text: It is slower, because each sale is looked up three times
choices.why: Speed is not the objection; the guess is.

choices.text: Python dictionaries cannot hold three optional keys
choices.why: They can; the problem is not in the dictionary.

choices.text: It spreads the guess about a sale's shape into more places
choices.why: Right. The next rename breaks it again; what is missing is a written agreement.

choices.text: Kafka would deliver sales with both fields twice
choices.why: Delivery has nothing to do with which field the reader looks for.

prompt: What does an Avro body contain, besides the values?

choices.text: The field names, before each value
choices.why: That is JSON. Avro writes no names at all.

choices.text: Nothing: the values in the schema's order
choices.why: Right. Only the schema says which value is which.

choices.text: A copy of the schema, compressed
choices.why: A Kafka message carries an id, not the schema; the body is values only.

choices.text: The names and the types of the fields, in a header
choices.why: There is no such header in the body; that is what the schema is for.

prompt: In `avro_demo.py`, how many bytes did the sale take as Avro?
A sale written with v1 is read with a reader schema that adds `till` with no default. What happens?

choices.text: `till` comes back as an empty string
choices.why: Avro does not invent a value; without a default there is nothing to use.

choices.text: `till` is left out of the result
choices.why: The reader asked for it, so it cannot simply be omitted.

choices.text: The read fails
choices.why: Right. v3 raised SchemaResolutionError: no default value for till.

choices.text: `till` is filled from the producer's configuration
choices.why: The producer did not write it; only a default in the reader's schema could fill it.

prompt: v2 renames `cents` to `amount` with `aliases: ["cents"]`. A consumer still on v1 receives a message written with v2. What happens?

choices.text: It reads `amount` as `cents`, thanks to the alias
choices.why: The alias is in the reader's schema of v2; a v1 reader does not have it.

choices.text: It fails, because it looks for `cents` and the writer had `amount`
choices.why: Right. An alias is the reader's knowledge of the past, so it only helps an upgraded reader.

choices.text: It reads the sale with `cents` set to zero
choices.why: Zero would need a default for `cents` in v1, which it does not have.

choices.text: The broker refuses to deliver it
choices.why: The broker never looks inside messages.

prompt: Where does the registry started in this lesson keep its schemas, and what follows from that?

choices.text: In a Kafka topic, so they survive a restart
choices.why: That is a production setting; with no configuration it uses memory.

choices.text: In memory, so stopping it forgets them
choices.why: Right. Fine for a lab; anywhere else it makes old messages unreadable.

choices.text: In `~/apicurio/registry.log`
choices.why: That file holds what the registry says about itself, not the schemas.

choices.text: In the broker's `__cluster_metadata` log
choices.why: Kafka does not know the registry exists.

prompt: Every client in this lesson is given `http://localhost:8080/apis/ccompat/v7`. Why that path?

choices.text: It is where Kafka serves its own schema API
choices.why: Kafka has no schema API; the registry is a separate service.

choices.text: Version 7 of Avro requires it in the address
choices.why: The v7 is the version of Confluent's API, not of Avro.

choices.text: Apicurio answers Confluent's API under it, so the Confluent client works unchanged
choices.why: Right. Confluent's own registry would be at port 8081 with no prefix.

choices.text: It turns on compatibility checking
choices.why: Compatibility is set per subject with `/config`; the path is just where the API lives.

prompt: Match each word to what it names in a schema registry.

pairs.right: the name a series of versions is kept under
the position of a schema within its subject
the number written into each message

right_distractors: the byte that is always zero

prompt: By convention, the subject for the values of the topic `sales-avro` is `sales-avro-___`.
`register.sh` offered `sale.avsc` a second time. What came back?

choices.text: A 409, because the schema already existed
choices.why: A repeated schema is not a conflict; it is recognised.

choices.text: The id 1 again, and no new version
choices.why: Right. That is what lets every producer offer its schema on start.

choices.text: Version 2 of the subject, with the same id
choices.why: The versions list stayed at [1] until a different schema arrived.

choices.text: A new id, 2, for the same schema
choices.why: The id belongs to the schema, so the same schema keeps id 1.

prompt: Put the bytes of a message value written by the Avro serialiser in order.
items: the length of the first string
the characters of the sale's id

prompt: How many bytes did the first message of partition 0 of `sales-avro` take, according to `od` (not counting the new line the console consumer adds)?
Why does `avro_tills.py` set `auto.register.schemas` to `False`?

choices.text: So that a producer cannot change the topic's schema by starting
choices.why: Right. Registering becomes a deliberate step, checked against the compatibility mode.

choices.text: Because Apicurio does not accept registrations from Python
choices.why: `register.sh` registered from the shell, and Python could too.

choices.text: To make each message smaller
choices.why: The message carries the same five-byte header either way.

choices.text: Because the serialiser would otherwise ask the registry for every message, at the full cost of an HTTP round trip each time
choices.why: The client caches what the registry tells it either way; the setting is about who may register.

prompt: `avro_tills.py` builds every sale with a `till` field, and `sale.avsc` has no such field. What does the serialiser do with it when given `sale.avsc`?

choices.text: Refuses the sale as not matching the schema
choices.why: Ten sales were sent with `sale.avsc`, each carrying `till`.

choices.text: Registers a new version that includes it
choices.why: Auto-registration is off, and the subject stayed at version 1.

choices.text: Writes it after the other fields, unnamed
choices.why: A field outside the schema has no position to be written at.

choices.text: Ignores it
choices.why: Right. It writes the fields its schema names, which lets one program write either version.

prompt: What compatibility mode did Apicurio's Confluent-compatible API report before anything was set?
hint: The first curl of the section printed it.

choices.text: `BACKWARD`
choices.why: That is Confluent's default, not Apicurio's.

choices.text: `FULL_TRANSITIVE`
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson's registry was that strict by default.

choices.text: `NONE`
choices.why: Right. It accepts any change until a mode is set.

choices.text: `FORWARD`
choices.why: The `/config` call answered with a different level.

prompt: Under `BACKWARD`, which of these changes to version 1 of the sale would the registry accept? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Adding `till` with a default
choices.why: Yes: it became version 2 with id 2.

choices.text: Removing the field `at`
choices.why: Yes: a new reader simply skips what old data has and it lacks.

choices.text: Renaming `cents` to `amount`
choices.why: Refused with a 409: it adds `amount` with no default.

choices.text: Adding `till` with no default
choices.why: A new reader could not fill it from an old sale.

prompt: A team uses `BACKWARD`. Version 2 removes a field and version 3 adds it back with another type; each was accepted. Why can version 3 still fail to read version 1 data?

choices.text: The check only compares a new schema with its predecessor
choices.why: Right. `BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE` checks against every earlier version and would have refused it.

choices.text: The registry forgot version 1 when version 3 arrived
choices.why: The registry only adds; version 1 is still there.

choices.text: Types can never change in Avro
choices.why: Some can, such as `int` to `long`; the issue is which versions were compared.

choices.text: Version 1 data was deleted by retention
choices.why: Even if it were still there, the problem is what the check compared.

prompt: Under `BACKWARD`, which side should be deployed first?

choices.text: The producers, so new data exists before readers look for it
choices.why: That is `FORWARD`'s order; under `BACKWARD` old readers may fail on new data.

choices.text: The consumers
choices.why: Right. A new reader can read old data, so readers move first.

choices.text: Neither: the registry deploys them together
choices.why: The registry checks schemas; it deploys nothing.

choices.text: Both at the same instant, or messages are lost
choices.why: No mode needs that; each says which side may go first.

prompt: After five sales were written with version 2, `avro_read.py` read the topic with `sale.avsc`. What did it show?

choices.text: Ten sales, because the reader skips versions it does not know
choices.why: It read all fifteen; the schema ids were {1: 10, 2: 5}.

choices.text: Fifteen sales, each with `till`
choices.why: `till` appeared only when it read with `sale-v2.avsc`.

choices.text: Fifteen sales, and no `till` in any of them
choices.why: Right. An old reader on new data gets the fields it asked for.

choices.text: An error on the first version 2 sale
choices.why: Adding a field with a default is safe in both directions.

prompt: What happens to the messages already in a topic when its schema gets a new version?

choices.text: They stay written with the version they were written with
choices.why: Right. A topic is not migrated; readers must cope with every version still in it.

choices.text: The registry rewrites them in the new version
choices.why: The registry never touches the topic.

choices.text: They are deleted at the next segment roll
choices.why: Deletion follows retention, not schema changes.

choices.text: Kafka marks them as outdated, and consumers skip them
choices.why: Kafka knows nothing about schemas.

prompt: Match each compatibility mode to who may upgrade first.
Ponto Final wants to rename `cents` to `amount` without breaking any reader. Which plan follows the lesson?

choices.text: Set the subject to `NONE`, register the rename, and deploy everything at night
choices.why: `NONE` only stops the registry from warning; old readers still break.

choices.text: Add `amount` beside `cents`, move readers to it, then remove `cents`
choices.why: Right. Slower, and it never breaks anybody.

choices.text: Rename it in the producer and rely on JSON to carry the new name
choices.why: That is the Monday at the start of the lesson.

choices.text: Delete the topic and start again with the new schema
choices.why: That throws away the history every reader depends on.
